source_anchor: FM-001 — Plan-only deliverable dropped; task mislabeled `stalled`
instance: Codex/Hermes wrote the consult answer as free prose above the CODEX REPORT ("Posted below is the assessment to send as the #54 comment") and reported status:done, but the poller only reads structured fields and still demanded a PR for a plan-only task; post-verify saw no PR and no recoverable field, so it applied agent/codex/stalled and the answer never reached issue #54.
check: Poller reads the plan-only label and routes a done task to deliver_plan_only, posting the report notes: field verbatim; an empty notes: yields stalled with an explanatory comment instead of a silent false done.

source_anchor: FM-002 — Double-claim window during poller cutover
instance: During a poller cutover from leviathan to codex.petersimmons.com, the old poller host still had a valid timer/service capable of claiming queue work while the new host was also enabled, creating a window where two consumers could both believe they were the sole active claimer of agent/codex/queued.
check: check_single_poller_namespace() reads scripts/config/fleet-hosts.txt at startup and fails hard if more than one host is declared active for the same CODEX_QUEUE_LABEL namespace; each poll cycle re-checks with warn-only. lease_write now runs before the claim PATCH to close the same-host race too.

source_anchor: FM-003 — Stale worktree/branch blocks re-claim (revert-to-queued loop)
instance: An issue's local git worktree/branch (agent/codex/issue-NN) lingered after a prior failed run; when the poller tried to reclaim the queued issue, git worktree add failed on the stale checkout, so the poller reverted the label to queued and retried later, hitting the identical stale-state failure in a loop.
check: Poller prunes its own stale worktrees/branches at the start of each claim; janitor self-prune ported to every fleet host (#63/#68).

source_anchor: FM-004 — Sandbox blocks the comms the task needs (egress + worktree `.git`)
instance: Inside the codex exec sandbox (bwrap workspace-write), network egress was blocked and the worktree's linked .git backing store was read-only, so an Engram auth health check failed (codex-doctor ok=false) and git commit failed with '.git/index.lock: Read-only file system' even though the task required both capabilities.
check: Deploy asserts sandbox_workspace_write network_access=true and writable_roots=["~/projects"] are present in config.toml; a post-deploy probe runs an in-sandbox Engram check plus a throwaway worktree commit and fails the cutover if either fails.

source_anchor: FM-005 — Consult queued to a non-existent agent label (silent mis-route)
instance: queue-agent --agent hermes tried to route a consult by naming an agent that had no corresponding GitHub label; GitHub rejected the label add ('agent/hermes' not found) and no running poller watched that route in the repo, so the consult silently failed to route.
check: queue-agent validates that the chosen agent's */queued label exists in the repo AND a running poller watches it, before creating the issue.

source_anchor: FM-006 — Issue-body prefetch silently empty → runner gets an empty prompt → misleading `needs-input`
instance: The host-side issue-body prefetch used `gh ... 2>/dev/null || echo ""`; under run-once the fetch returned empty and that empty string fell through silently into the rendered prompt's 'Issue body:' section, causing codex to correctly but misleadingly ask the human to paste the body after a ~75s run.
check: Prefetch failure now surfaces disposition=failed with stderr and never launches codex on an empty prompt.

source_anchor: FM-007 — Failure-shape promotion: a missing-artifact failure inferred as a plan deliverable
instance: A proposed fix treated the shape 'status=done + notes + no PR + no commits' as proof of a plan-only deliverable, but red-team review (Hermes) showed that exact shape is indistinguishable from an impl run that narrated intent but produced nothing — inferring success from absence of an artifact would silently promote real failures to success.
check: Adversarial test: an impl/default task reporting done + notes + no PR must be FAILED, not delivered, unless an explicit producer-set expected_delivery signal marks it plan-only.

source_anchor: FM-008 — Delivery gated on a side-channel signal the producer never sets
instance: fleet_run_once routed delivery to deliver_plan_only only if the GitHub issue carried the agent/codex/plan-only label, but items enqueued via fleet-dispatch's capability-keyed path (capability=review) never set that label, so a valid done+notes result hit the no-artifact guard and was discarded.
check: Explicit-signal plan-only delivery test: routing reads the same key the producer sets (capability/explicit enqueue field), not a side-channel GitHub label.

source_anchor: FM-009 — Webhook → notifier dropped; node gets no wake but 30-min fallback catches it
instance: A GitHub issues.labeled webhook delivery failed silently (Ingress down, DNS gap, or notifier pod crash), so fleet-notifier never emitted a wake to the target node's SSE stream; the node fell back to waiting up to 30 minutes for the systemd timer with no alert firing on the gap.
check: Notifier exposes a last_webhook_received_ts metric; alert fires if no webhook is received within N x expected-label-interval while open issues exist.

source_anchor: FM-010 — Notifier → node SSE missed during reconnect window
instance: fleet-notifier pushed a wake to a node's SSE stream at the exact moment the node's connection was reconnecting; SSE has no guaranteed replay, so the wake was permanently lost and not recoverable from the stream on reconnect.
check: Wake is made level-triggered via a durable per-node dirty-bit/monotonic wake-seq cleared only after the node reports successful drain-to-empty; a reconnect re-reads the current level and triggers one immediate drain.

source_anchor: FM-011 — Signal beats the GitHub write; node fetches ref → 404
instance: A sender POSTed a consult-ready signal immediately after GitHub API returned 201 for the referenced artifact, but GitHub's eventual-consistency replication lagged, so the target node's GET /repos/.../issues/NNN returned 404 because the artifact was not yet visible on the replica it hit.
check: Receiver retries the fetch with exponential backoff before giving up and never acts on signal-carried data, only on what GitHub returns; unresolved ref after max retries falls back to the 30-min poller.

source_anchor: FM-012 — Auth gap: unauthenticated or spoofed POST accepted, emitting unauthorized wake
instance: If fleet-notifier's HMAC (webhook path) or per-node token (consult path) validation is absent or misconfigured, an unauthenticated or spoofed POST could pass through and emit a wake indistinguishable from a legitimate one, turning the notification bus into an unauthenticated authority channel.
check: Webhook path rejects invalid HMAC with 401 and no wake; consult path requires a per-node token cryptographically bound to from_node; every accepted signal appends an audit record; identity-bind failure drops closed.

source_anchor: FM-013 — Wake storm: N rapid label events produce N redundant drains → GitHub rate-limit
instance: A bulk enqueue of ~50 issues rapidly emitted 50 issues.labeled webhook deliveries; without debounce, fleet-notifier forwarded 50 wakes and the node performed 50 concurrent/rapid drains (50x list+claim API calls), triggering GitHub secondary rate-limiting even though each individual hop behaved correctly.
check: Per-node debounce window at the notifier collapses N label events into <=1 wake per window; a single drain must clear all N queued items.

source_anchor: FM-014 — Notifier total outage: no fallback path triggers; SSE failure silently disables the 30-min timer
instance: When fleet-notifier is scaled to 0 or crashed, an SSE failure handler could incorrectly disable the fallback 30-min systemd timer (e.g. calling systemctl stop on reconnect failure), turning a bus outage that should only regress latency into an indefinite work-stoppage.
check: The 30-min systemd timer is armed at all times and is never stopped/disabled by the SSE client on any error path; SSE is additive, the timer is the floor.

source_anchor: FM-015 — Liveness ≠ ownership: partition makes a live node look dead; coordinator reassigns in-progress work
instance: A network partition dropped node A's heartbeats to the notifier while node A was still alive and working its claimed issue; the coordinator inferred node A was dead from missing heartbeats and reassigned the in-progress issue to node B, producing dual ownership and possible conflicting outputs on the same GitHub issue.
check: Coordinator verifies the durable GitHub claim (label + lease record) is expired or explicitly released before reassigning; bus liveness is used only for routing new work, never to revoke in-progress ownership.

source_anchor: FM-016 — Wrong consumer token: `consumes:["plan"]` in grok container → silent eternal empty-claim loop
instance: grok.env was provisioned with the coordinator-impl FLEET_DISPATCH_TOKEN (node=coordinator-impl, consumes=["plan"]) instead of the grok consumer token (consumes=["impl-grok"]); grok-attach's /claim calls correctly returned {"empty":true} forever since no plan items existed, and the container stayed running and healthy with zero error output, starving silently.
check: ONCE=1 canary run after every token change; {"empty":true} on a known non-empty queue is the diagnostic. Verify token identity via fingerprint (sha256/12) + GET /whoami against Infisical, never by printing the bearer value.

source_anchor: FM-017 — Missing `expected_delivery=comment_only` → artifact gate 422 on every `done` report
instance: fleet-enqueue.sh's build_request_body() had no expected_delivery parameter, so it never sent expected_delivery=comment_only for impl-grok/impl-opencode items; every done report from those comment-only consumers hit fleet-dispatch's artifact gate and was rejected with HTTP 422 'done/needs-input report must include branch and head_sha', failing on every retry.
check: Delivery contracts must distinguish comment-only reports from branch artifacts; verify successful report acknowledgement.

source_anchor: FM-018 — Stale queued items → ONCE=1 canary claims old items; clean test never runs
instance: Repeated ONCE=1 canary runs kept claiming stale test items from prior failed runs (e4daa9c2, 6b41b54d, f40a9457) instead of the freshly enqueued canary, because fleet-dispatch /claim correctly returns items in FIFO order and abandoned items had re-queued after lease TTL expiry, some hitting 409 'stale fence' on report.
check: Cancel all existing queued items for the capability under test (POST /item/{id}/cancel) before starting an ONCE=1 canary run, so exactly one fresh item exists in queue.

source_anchor: FM-019 — Container running stale image: fix merged to main but host never rebuilt → old binary in production
instance: After PR #244 (XAI_API_KEY unbound-variable fix) merged to main, the grok host's GROK_ATTACH_ENABLED gate flip + container restart ran from the cached Docker image rather than rebuilding, so grok-attach kept hitting 'XAI_API_KEY: unbound variable' on every task and every canary item reported failed despite the fix being present in main.
check: Activation sequence is always: git pull origin main -> docker compose build -> docker compose up -d -> ONCE=1 canary confirms 'reported done'; skipping the build step is the failure.

source_anchor: FM-020 — `impl-grok` dead-letters with empty output; failure is flaky, not a simple payload-size threshold
instance: Of four impl-grok prose-review jobs (~3KB-~260KB), one ~3KB job succeeded while another ~3KB job of similar size failed identically 3/3 times with 'grok produced empty output' or a tool_error/list_dir/tool_output_error, showing the failure was real flakiness in the grok execution path rather than a payload-size threshold.
check: scripts/fleet-canary.sh supports comment-only capabilities (including impl-grok) via auto-set expected_delivery=comment_only and a non-mutating prompt, turning a silently broken lane into a fast explicit failure before a live batch is enqueued.

source_anchor: FM-021 — `review` capability items remained queued for hours with empty `lease_holder`; no consumer ever claimed them
instance: Five review-capability items (a8e97eed, f2ee6323, b10075b1, 01b7d02e, 18ca5cdc) sat in state:queued with lease_holder:"" and retries:0 for more than two hours with no claim-then-fail signature at all, indicating a missing/misbound live consumer for that capability with no alert surfacing the starvation.
check: scripts/fleet-canary.sh enforces CANARY_CLAIM_TIMEOUT / --claim-timeout and fails with a queued-but-never-claimed error including lease_holder, retries, capability, and item id.

source_anchor: FM-022 — `comment_only` artifact-gate exemption is disposition-scoped, not delivery-scoped: a `needs-input` clarifying question still forces a git artifact
instance: fleet-dispatch's validateArtifactWithDelivery only exempts branch/head_sha inside case DispositionDone (queue.go:1615-1623); case DispositionNeedsInput (queue.go:1624-1631) never reads expectedDelivery and unconditionally requires branch/head_sha, so item f94a06c4-4d5b-4247-9d8a-1b4fba6926b0 (a comment_only-style consult reporting needs-input with a text-only clarifying question) was forced to carry a fabricated branch/head_sha.
check: Planned queue.go unit test asserting validateArtifactWithDelivery(DispositionNeedsInput, {Question:...}, "comment_only") returns nil (no artifact required), mirroring the existing done-case exemption test.

source_anchor: FM-023 — `needs-input` handoff with an empty question replays the entire expensive work step
instance: Items 3b140900 (codex#153) and c8d4e365 (codex#152) each completed and committed real work then reported needs-input, but fleet-dispatch's §6.3.1 validation found the question empty after trimming (the parser had read failure_reason: and ignored the protocol's needs: field, and codex-attach copied result_ref into question without validating it was non-empty), so the item was downgraded and re-queued, causing the node to re-execute the entire work step from scratch until retries exhausted while a container healthcheck also false-tripped UNHEALTHY on the resulting long-running (6-9 min) active work step.
check: codex-poll.sh maps the needs: field into the parsed failure/question slot; codex-attach.sh downgrades needs-input with an empty trimmed question to failed before /report instead of emitting an invalid envelope; healthcheck.sh treats current_item!=null as active work and allows MAX_WORK_DURATION + freshness slack before flagging staleness.
